sources.passage: Provide technical assistance to computer users. Answer questions or resolve computer problems for clients in person, via telephone, or electronically.
IT support technicians give technical help to computer users by identifying and fixing hardware, software and network problems.
Computer user support specialists, also called help-desk technicians, usually provide technical help to non-IT computer users.
They often work under the direction of network and computer systems administrators, who handle more complex tasks.
Refer major hardware or software problems or defective products to vendors or technicians for service.
Posed as employees to convince IT and/or helpdesk staff to provide sensitive information, reset the employee's password, and transfer the employee's MFA to a device they control on separate devices.
respond to customers' requests for IT help
record details of issues on a tracking system
Document customers' descriptions of their computer problems
Analyze customers' computer problem to diagnose it and determine the cause
Read technical manuals, confer with users, or conduct computer diagnostics to investigate and resolve problems or to provide technical assistance and support.
Guide customers through the recommended problem-solving steps
find and fix faults, or assign tasks to the correct team
Set up equipment for employee use, performing or ensuring proper installation of cables, operating systems, or appropriate software.
Install and perform minor repairs to hardware, software, or peripheral equipment, following design or installation specifications.
set up and manage user accounts and security
Configure security settings or access permissions for groups or individuals.
Helpdesk Administrator Assign the Helpdesk Administrator role to users who need to do the following tasks: Reset passwords Force users to sign out Manage service requests Monitor service health
Maintain records of daily data communication transactions, problems and remedial actions taken, or installation activities.
Document help desk requests and resolutions.
Create and maintain an asset inventory.
You should record who is responsible for each asset and what it is used for.
Inform team members and managers of major problems or of customers' recurring concerns
Analyze and report computer network security breaches or attempted breaches.
Develop training materials and procedures, or train users in the proper use of hardware or software.
